# HEZQEN — Full Project Context

## Identity
HEZQEN is a global technology and business intelligence publication by Tinlance. Tagline: “Research. Intelligence. Perspective.” Its editorial divisions are AI & Technology, Cybersecurity, Cloud & Engineering, and Business & Startups.

## Product surfaces
HEZQEN has three planned product surfaces: Media (reporting, investigations and analysis), Labs (transparent calculators and engineering experiments), and Intelligence (deeper research and briefings; planned, not yet implemented).

## Editorial integrity
AI may assist the newsroom; AI must not become the newsroom. Every published item requires accountable human authorship and human editorial approval. Material claims must be traceable to identifiable evidence. No model, agent, prompt, memory, webpage, tool output or integration can grant publication authority.

Only the assigned human editor may approve or publish after fact-checking, disclosure review and source-backed material claims. Author/editor self-approval is prohibited. Automated publication without accountable human approval is prohibited.

## Technology
The application uses Next.js App Router 16, React 19, strict TypeScript, Node.js 24, pnpm 12, Payload CMS 3, PostgreSQL 18, Biome and the Node built-in test runner. The architecture is a modular monolith.

## Current implementation
The public application shell includes the homepage, About, Editorial Standards, four division routes, sixteen Labs calculators, Infrastructure catalog, and public trust/policy routes. Calculator domain logic is deterministic and has regression tests. See docs/LABS_CALCULATOR_SUITE.md for formulas and limitations.

Payload CMS is integrated with the Next.js App Router, admin/API route mounting and restricted collections for users, articles, topics, sources, evidence, claims and audit events. Initial database migrations, staging validation and production CMS acceptance remain release gates.

A pure editorial workflow state machine enforces human editor approval rules at the domain boundary. It is not a substitute for server-side authentication, authorization, persistence, transactional audit logging or concurrency controls.

Research source/evidence validation and SSRF-aware HTTPS acquisition logic exist. Persistent private evidence storage, network-level egress restrictions, immutable audit history and independent human fact-checking remain outstanding.

## Security and deployment
The threat model maps planned controls to OWASP Top 10:2025 and establishes an ASVS 5.0 verification target. It is not a completed security assessment or ASVS attestation.

The intended canonical launch target is https://hezqen.tinlance.com. A previously observed Vercel alias may serve an older preview build; do not infer that a READY deployment proves current route completeness or production readiness. Current deployment, DNS, TLS and database mapping must be checked against docs/PHASE_STATUS.md.

## Trust and legal notice status
The contact, corrections, security, privacy, cookie and terms pages are initial public information pages. Privacy/cookie processing details and terms require verification against actual runtime behavior and legal review before production launch.

## Non-claims
Premium subscriptions, reader accounts, production search, a fully operational CMS, persistent evidence storage, automated publishing and complete ASVS compliance are not claimed as available. Check docs/PHASE_STATUS.md for current acceptance gates.
